chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The post-partum woman sits [abstaining from prayer] for the days of her menstruation which she used to menstruate, then she examines herself, and she performs the ritual bath and prays.'

key_terms.تَسْتَظْهِرُ: She examines herself (to check for purity)

ai.seo_question: How does a post-partum woman determine when to resume prayer after childbirth?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of nufas by linking it to the woman's habitual menstrual cycle, a principle rooted in the Prophetic tradition that postpartum bleeding ceases when the usual period ends. It emphasizes the procedural necessity of istihaza (self-examination) and ghusl before resuming Salah, reflecting the Shia scholarly consensus on distinguishing between nufas and hayd based on duration and purity signs.
